Coverage of the point immediately above would tend to correct what we feel is an overstatement where you say "Insofar as habitat improvement for the benefit of one species generally enhances the environment for other species, this legislation will improve the environment for all species..." Is it not true that in at least some instances certain species would be displaced by the type of habitat which is developed? It follows, then, that environment for "all species" will not be improved.
In your discussion of brown pelican you imply that "The physical intrusion of 'any large animal' may so disturb the nesting birds that they will abandon the nest". Pernaps you have overstated the case to make a point concerning man's activities. We feel that the objectivity you display elsewhere in discussing interrelationships within ecosystems should be evidenced here, too.
Under "Mitigating Measures", you devote most of the text to protection of the animals and impact on economy and use. We ask for consideration of ecosystems involved and general measures affecting land and water. Our rationale for asking this has been thoroughly discussed above.
If the goals of this proposal are to be accomplished, there will be commitments of resources. Most obvious are land and water; in some instances certain species which have been displaced by endangered forms will suffer a reduction in range and loss in total population size. These points should be included in your section on "Irreversible and Irretrievable Commitments of Resource Which Would Be Involved In The Proposed Action Should It Be Implemented". Our suggestion is not based on whether this commitment is good or bad, but on the need to recognize it.
Our only comment on alternatives will be limited to the suggestion that you seriously consider the material covered in our points 1 thru 4 in the first part of this response. Rather than listing as an alternate, we sk that they be included within your primary proposal and become a part of your program.
We commend you for this important action of great interest and concern to citizens of the United States. Our many suggestions are sincerely intended to assist you in preparing your final draft, which we will look forward to receiving.
Sincerely,
THE DEPARTMENT OF GAME
Eugene S. Dziedzic, Asst. Chief Environmental Management Division
E.S. Oughtic
